title: How ABS stops a car's wheels locking
examples: Why does the brake pedal shudder when I brake hard?
How does ABS know a wheel is skidding?

explain.say: If you brake very hard, a wheel can stop turning while the car is still moving. A locked wheel skids, and a skidding tyre cannot steer. The anti-lock braking system, ABS, stops that happening.

explain.say: A sensor at each wheel tells a computer how fast the wheel is turning. If one wheel suddenly slows far faster than the car possibly could, the computer knows that wheel is about to lock.

faq.q: How does ABS know a wheel is locking?
faq.a: Each wheel has a speed sensor, usually a magnetic sensor reading a toothed ring. The computer compares the wheels, and one slowing much faster than the rest is about to lock.

faq.q: What does the ABS computer do?
faq.a: It watches all the wheel speeds hundreds of times a second. When one wheel starts to lock it orders the valves to ease and reapply that brake.
asks: Is ABS controlled by a computer?

faq.q: How does ABS release the brakes?
faq.a: Valves in the ABS unit can hold, lower or raise the brake fluid pressure to each wheel separately. Lowering it for an instant lets a locking wheel roll again.
asks: What does the ABS valve do?

faq.q: Why is a rolling wheel better than a skidding one?
faq.a: A rolling tyre grips with static friction, which is stronger than the sliding friction of a skid, and it can grip sideways, so the car still steers.
asks: Why does a skidding car not steer?

faq.q: Why does the brake pedal pulse with ABS?
faq.a: The pulsing is the ABS valves and pump easing and reapplying the pressure many times a second. It is normal: keep your foot pressed down firmly and steer.
asks: Is it bad if the brake pedal vibrates?

facts: ABS can ease and reapply the brakes many times a second, far faster than any driver could.
The main benefit of ABS is that the driver can still steer while braking hard.
On loose gravel or deep snow, ABS can make stopping distances a little longer, though the car can still be steered.
